task_title: Spot the concurrency race in session-token attribution
output:
(1) Non-atomic before/after set-diff race (TOCTOU) on a shared session store: `new_ids` is not owned by the caller.

(2) Threads A and B both snapshot the same `before`. Each creates one session. When A samples `after`, both sessions are present, so `new_ids` has two IDs and `max(new_ids)` can pick B’s session. A’s 19k-token run is then scored with B’s ~200-token export. Same-prompt runs cannot be told apart by content.

(3) Fix: make ownership explicit — have `run_cli` return `session_id`, or tag the session with a per-call UUID and look that up. Else hold a mutex around snapshot→run→diff, or give each worker an isolated session store. Do not infer via global set diff + `max`.

judgeDetail.rationale: Nails the non-atomic diff race, the A/B max()-picks-wrong-session mechanism, the same-prompt disambiguation note, and offers real race-removing fixes (return id / UUID tag / mutex), all concrete and line-specific.
